title: Perfect local lifting of a lisse residue reduction
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact) [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-pc-scheme]. Let $(A,I)$ be an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and assume $A\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/I^n$. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and inverse limits of sheaves [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Put $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/I^n)_X$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $M\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] be derived $I$-complete [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. Suppose $M_1=M\otimes^L_{B_X}(A/I)_X$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] is etale locally on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] isomorphic to the constant complex of a perfect $A/I$-complex: there is an etale covering on each member of which $M_1$ is isomorphic, after pullback to the pro-etale site, to a bounded complex of constant sheaves of finite projective $A/I$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Then there is a pro-etale covering $\{U_j\to X\}$ and perfect $A$-complexes $P_j$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], meaning bounded complexes of finite projective $A$-modules, with $M|_{U_j}\simeq B_X|_{U_j}\otimes_A^L P_j$. Here tensor with $A$ means tensor with its constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and restriction is to the corresponding localized site. No stratification or compatible etale witnesses are asserted in this conclusion.

source.place: Tag 09C6, lemma-connected-adic-lisse, applied on connected open components of a Noetherian scheme; coefficient change by lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence. Also literature/bhatt-scholze-pro-etale-topology_arXiv-1309.1198.pdf, Lemma 6.6.8 and Proposition 6.6.11, local lifting ingredient.

proof.text: Construct the normalized constant-to-finite coefficient comparison by the sheafification adjunction. The finite coefficient scalar map is locally injective and locally surjective, hence its induced sheaf map is invertible. Adjunction proves the constant-section formula and uniqueness. Choose bounded finite-projective representatives for each residue witness and use exact constant-functor localization factors to replace its derived constant image by the actual constant complex. The finite coefficient comparisons are proved compatible with consecutive quotient maps and completed scalar projections by testing on constant sections.

Apply the uniform finite quotient models lemma to these representatives and normalized coefficient comparisons. This proves finite-level local perfect models with a uniform interval on each initial etale chart; no completeness hypothesis is used in this step. The finite-level theorem proves the zero case by further exact slice restriction and then inducts with the one-step coefficient-filtration lemma, retaining the interval [min a b,b].

Apply finite perfect adic realization to this finite-level structure. It identifies the derived inverse limit of the actual strict quotient tower, on one pro-etale cover, with completed realization of a bounded finite-projective A-complex.

The unit-compatible Koszul reconstruction comparison makes the quotient-completion unit invertible on the intrinsically complete M. Exact slice restriction transports this isomorphism; its localization factors compare the functorial restriction with the representative-based object in the statement. Compose with the preceding local limit identification and with the exact constant-complex localization comparison. The chosen bounded finite-projective A-complex has perfect image in D(A).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NE-f3cabda4a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: The delivery is one commit, and its only change to the item is status unsplit→split. The statement, the six steps and the recorded tool_uses are the text NB's reviewer already passed on 2026-10-14, and the new status now agrees with that review. There are no new nodes. I re-read the whole item anyway, against the statement of every cited node, Stacks 09C6 (with 094I, 09AW and 099M) and Bhatt–Scholze 6.6.8 and 6.6.11. The coefficient category stays D(Mod(B_X)) throughout; it is compared with constant A only through restriction of scalars in the constant-completion equivalence. The statement is the form its only citer needs (step 5 of integral-stratified-perfect-characterization), nothing is weakened, and the edge cases I = A, I = 0, empty X and Z_ℓ hold. Step 2 proves by induction on n that every M_n is bounded with finite locally constant cohomology, using the weak Serre lemma over the Noetherian ring A/I^{n+1}. Step 3, the flagged 2134-character step, is one argument and may stay: it builds the étale origins L_n and lifts the normalization maps to them. Its one delicate point is handled correctly: A/I^n has infinite Tor dimension over A/I^{n+1}, so L_{n+1} ⊗^L A/I^n need not be bounded below; the step shows it is bounded (ν^* is exact and its unit reflects zero sheaves) before using full faithfulness on D^+. It also checks the hypotheses of nilpotent-reduction lissity (J^n = 0, bounded above). Step 4 checks the hypotheses of 09AW, including I-adic completeness of A. Step 5's isomorphism sheaves are finite locally constant and have nonempty stalks because Y is connected. Step 6's Roos computation, surjective sections and the transfer of isomorphisms through TR3 are all correct. The route stays in the unit apart from the accepted generic tool_uses, and no SGA is cited. One small note: the report mentions a citations.json that is not in the commit; this does not affect the DAG. No fixes were made.
